subject.title: Expose maxMissedJobsPerRestart and missedJobStaggerMs in cron config

question: Should OpenClaw expose restart catch-up controls in public cron config, and should the supported shape be the existing global max/stagger knobs, a skip/catch-up policy, or no new public config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but root policy treats new config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive and the choice changes scheduler semantics for existing cron users after gateway restarts.

options.title: Expose Narrow Global Controls
options.body: Approve documented `cron.maxMissedJobsPerRestart` and `cron.missedJobStaggerMs` keys, including zero-limit disable semantics, while preserving current defaults for existing users.

options.title: Design A Policy Surface
options.body: Use a global or per-job skip/catch-up policy instead of exposing the raw internal dependency names, with defaults that preserve current behavior.

options.title: Keep Controls Internal
options.body: Decline new public config for now and document current restart catch-up behavior, limits, and operational workarounds.

recommendation.title: Expose Narrow Global Controls
recommendation.body: Approve documented `cron.maxMissedJobsPerRestart` and `cron.missedJobStaggerMs` keys, including zero-limit disable semantics, while preserving current defaults for existing users.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available decision owner from history because he committed the original internal catch-up controls and has adjacent cron startup-flow history.
